title: Prototype result: useful reach warnings, alignment remains unreliable
conclusion: Not ready for automatic image acceptance. Scores and verdicts are provisional.
findings: 18 final target images: 8 development images and 10 held-out images. Five fixed visual examples are shown separately; their three development case families are excluded from target evaluation.

On held-out data, all three specifically attributed reach complaints were detected. One of those comments also identified an alignment problem that the judge missed (3 of 4 mapped defect types detected across those three comments).

Of two other held-out alignment comments with no named variant, one had a matching issue detected in at least one candidate; the other was missed in both. This is comparison-set evidence, not exact-image agreement.

Held-out verdicts: 7 pass, 3 review, 0 fail. Row13 V14 received 92.5/pass despite a human alignment complaint. Row26 received 100/pass in both versions despite the comparison-level alignment complaint.

No human absolute placement ratings or reliable negative labels exist in these snapshots. Do not interpret these counts as accuracy, sensitivity over production data, specificity or calibrated threshold performance.
scoring_note: Severity0–4 converts to component scores100,75,50,25,0. Weighted average excludes unobservable components; coverage and confidence are separate. A clear major issue vetoes an overall pass. Partial observations do not certify hidden details.
limitations: Small purposive pilot; three exact-target held-out comment records, no gold absolute scores, possible shared device/view families. V14 scene-stage provenance is supported by code/report lineage but lacks a complete raw-PNG artifact chain. Confidence labels are model-derived, not calibrated probabilities. GPT-5.5 high with fixed visual examples averaged52.9seconds per held-out image in this run.
